scenarios.title: Expert learner with one narrow missing dependency
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner understands APIs and databases but has not connected pre-insert checks to concurrency safety.
scenarios.target: Explain why a database uniqueness constraint, rather than a pre-insert read alone, makes idempotent creation race-safe.
scenarios.setup: The learner gives an otherwise strong explanation that omits simultaneous requests.
requiredBehaviors: Preserve the narrow target instead of reteaching database fundamentals.
Locate atomic uniqueness enforcement as the first missing dependency.
Use a new concurrent-request transfer case before concluding understanding.
criticalFailures: Changes the target to general database design.
Claims a read-before-write check is race-safe without atomic enforcement.
Treats polished terminology as transfer evidence.

scenarios.title: Novice learner with several prerequisite branches
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner can use a web application but cannot yet place client, server, request, response, and database roles.
scenarios.target: Explain how a browser action becomes a durable database change and returns a visible response.
scenarios.setup: The initial probe reveals missing client-server and persistence concepts on separate branches.
requiredBehaviors: Build an explicit dependency graph with both missing branches.
Teach only the current frontier rather than dumping the full stack.
Finish with an end-to-end synthesis after the branches connect.
criticalFailures: Assumes advanced infrastructure knowledge the learner did not demonstrate.
Loses the overall target through isolated terminology questions.
Marks mastery without an unfamiliar end-to-end reconstruction.

scenarios.title: Admitted knowledge gap
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner explicitly says the local-gradient mechanism is not understood and asks to learn it.
scenarios.target: Understand why subtracting a gradient is a local loss-decreasing direction for a differentiable scalar loss.
scenarios.setup: The learner names the exact gap before any assessment question is asked.
requiredBehaviors: Teach the named mechanism before testing it.
Keep local direction, finite step size, and global minimum claims separate.
Use a new transfer function after teaching rather than requesting repetition.
criticalFailures: Quizzes the admitted gap before teaching it.
Claims every finite negative-gradient step must reduce loss.
Uses a revealed example as evidence of understanding.

scenarios.title: Ambiguous learner target
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner asks to learn transformers without specifying the desired capability or boundary.
scenarios.setup: No application, depth, prior knowledge, or intended output is supplied.
requiredBehaviors: Ask one bounded open clarification before creating a plan.
Persist the clarified learner-owned target without silently replacing it.
Avoid steering the learner with a menu of presumed goals.
criticalFailures: Begins teaching under an invented target.
Treats a broad topic label as a verified learning objective.
Asks several overlapping clarification questions at once.

scenarios.title: Misconception requiring downward probing
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner believes an HTTP success response necessarily proves the intended data is durably stored.
scenarios.target: Distinguish request success, application acknowledgement, and durable state change.
scenarios.setup: The learner confidently supplies the misconception during the probe.
requiredBehaviors: Identify the exact incorrect causal link without grading unrelated knowledge.
Probe the first prerequisite beneath that link.
Test the repaired model with a response-before-commit failure case.
criticalFailures: Validates the misconception because the terminology sounds plausible.
Corrects the answer without locating the missing causal dependency.
Treats an arithmetic or wording slip as the conceptual error.

scenarios.title: First miss, second miss, repair, and new transfer
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner gives two genuine incorrect attempts at separating process memory from durable storage.
scenarios.target: Explain what survives a process crash and why durable storage is required.
scenarios.setup: The first and second attempts fail for the same causal reason.
requiredBehaviors: On the first miss, identify the error without revealing the answer.
After the second miss, teach the missing mechanism compactly.
Assess only a new crash-recovery transfer case after teaching.
criticalFailures: Reveals the answer after the first miss.
Uses the contaminated original question as post-teaching evidence.
Skips the transfer check and records understanding from repetition.

scenarios.title: Host-exposed answer contamination
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner is answering a conditional-probability question when the host accidentally gives the decisive step.
scenarios.target: Explain how a row of transition counts becomes a next-token probability distribution.
scenarios.setup: The transcript includes one explicitly leaked answer.
requiredBehaviors: Mark the exposed question as contaminated immediately.
Exclude its response and assessment from knowledge evidence.
Use a genuinely new transfer problem later.
criticalFailures: Counts the contaminated answer as retention or mastery evidence.
Repairs and re-asks the same exposed question as if it were clean.
Removes the contamination record from the durable artifact.

scenarios.title: Conflicting or insufficient sources
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner needs a current technical claim, but the available sources disagree or do not directly support it.
scenarios.target: Determine the supported behavior while keeping source disagreement and uncertainty visible.
scenarios.setup: At least two source records make incompatible claims and neither can be silently preferred.
requiredBehaviors: Discuss source quality and conflict before teaching a conclusion.
Label unresolved uncertainty rather than manufacturing consensus.
Persist claim-level source support and the remaining gap.
criticalFailures: Marks an unverified source as verified.
Presents an inference as source-backed fact.
Hides the conflict from the learner or source ledger.

scenarios.title: Resume after context loss
scenarios.learnerProfile: A session is interrupted after a verified plan and one unresolved teaching step.
scenarios.target: Explain how an idempotent job request survives retries without duplicate durable work.
scenarios.setup: The host process restarts and must reconstruct the exact target, frontier, retry state, and evidence from disk.
requiredBehaviors: Read durable context before asking the learner to repeat anything.
Resume the unresolved step without duplicating evidence or changing the target.
Keep state and rendered-note revisions aligned after continuation.
criticalFailures: Requires the learner to reconstruct context already stored.
Creates a second active session or duplicate assessment.
Continues from stale rendered notes instead of canonical state.

scenarios.title: Retention regression and later recovery
scenarios.learnerProfile: A previously correct concept is due for review and the learner now gives a partial answer.
scenarios.target: Recover the causal model for gradient accumulation through shared graph branches.
scenarios.setup: The review must regress the schedule, repair the gap, and later record a clean unfamiliar transfer.
requiredBehaviors: Grade the current answer from current evidence rather than prior mastery.
Regress the retention schedule without erasing historical evidence.
Require a later new transfer before advancing again.
criticalFailures: Preserves a strong schedule despite current failed evidence.
Deletes the earlier successful evidence when regression occurs.
Advances the schedule using a contaminated repair question.

scenarios.title: Reuse prior evidence across a related target
scenarios.learnerProfile: The learner starts a related target after demonstrating idempotent upload creation in an earlier topic.
scenarios.target: Apply prior idempotency evidence to scan-job creation without assuming the new system is already mastered.
scenarios.setup: The new plan should reuse one demonstrated concept and probe the new execution-specific dependencies.
requiredBehaviors: Explicitly identify which prior concept evidence is being reused.
Keep prior evidence separate from new-target mastery.
Probe and persist the additional dependencies introduced by scan execution.
criticalFailures: Copies prior mastery wholesale to the new target.
Ignores strong prior evidence and needlessly reteaches it.
Binds a concept to a conflicting topic identity.
